title.zh: 经验快离子阻止截面增量

summary: Evaluate one fixed empirical additive fast-ion contribution to the neutral-beam stopping cross section from local power density, supplied electron slowing time and a magnetic-axis birth-pitch cosine; return only the increment in m^2.

capability: A local additive area contribution evaluated with supplied power density and electron slowing time.
operation: Evaluate a fixed empirical additive stopping contribution
beam mass and energy, birth-pitch cosine, electron density and temperature, local power density and slowing time -> stopping increment in m^2
discovery.model: Fixed empirical energy and pitch polynomials, fractional temperature power and pitch-diffusion parameter y=0.6; this is expression evaluation with no established quantitative calibration interval or fit-error bound.
discovery.geometry: Caller-supplied cosine of the neutral-particle birth direction relative to the magnetic axis; scalar inputs become (1,1), vectors become rows and lower-rank arrays gain singleton axes on the right. No beam path, magnetic field or spatial geometry is reconstructed.
discovery.boundary: The expression uses fmin(1,abs(birth_pitch_cosine)), including NaN pitch mapping to one, and overwrites only the energy polynomial for energy_ratio>pi. Other zero, negative, nonfinite and extreme real inputs retain arithmetic warnings and NaN/Inf/complex outcomes; complex inputs and incompatible axes fail.

identity.relation: a fixed empirical additive fast-ion contribution to the neutral-beam stopping cross section
identity.direction: seven local beam/plasma inputs -> stopping_increment_m2 array
identity.definition: Let A=beam_mass_number, E=beam_energy_ev, c=birth_pitch_cosine, n=electron_density_m3, te=electron_temperature_ev, P=power_density_w_m3 and tau=electron_slowing_time_s. Use e=1.602176462e-19 J/eV, S=P/(E*e), T=(te/1e3)/10, Ehat=(E/A)/1e6 and r=Ehat/T. Accumulate F(r)=0.57658+1.6432*r-4.8886*r^2+5.3932*r^3-2.9226*r^4+0.77156*r^5-0.079095*r^6 in ascending power order, then overwrite F with zero where r>pi, leaving equality unchanged. Set p=fmin(1,abs(c)); NaN c therefore gives p=1. Accumulate G(p)=0.30812*p+11.992*p^2-68.971*p^3+165.94*p^4-177.33*p^5+69.833*p^6 in ascending power order. With fixed pitch-diffusion parameter y=0.6, form R=(((T^(-0.9027)*F(r))*G(p))*1e-19 m^2, then return ((S*tau)/n)*R, retaining this multiplication/division order and the complex fractional-power branch for negative T. S has units m^-3 s^-1, S*tau/n is dimensionless and 1e-19 m^2 supplies the area scale.
identity.model: fixed empirical polynomials and temperature power with pitch diffusion fixed at y=0.6; no calibrated prediction over a quantified physical domain
identity.geometry: local supplied quantities and a magnetic-axis birth-pitch cosine; no spatial or magnetic geometry solver
identity.coordinates: E and te in eV, n in m^-3, P in W/m^3 and tau in s; A and the birth-pitch cosine are dimensionless. Scalar inputs become (1,1), one-dimensional inputs become (1,N), and implicit expansion aligns leading axes by appending singleton axes on the right.
identity.boundary: only the absolute pitch cap and strict r>pi energy-polynomial overwrite are applied; there is no density gate, finite-result guarantee or zero-power short circuit
assumptions: The coefficient tables, ascending-power accumulation, e=1.602176462e-19 J/eV and fixed y=0.6 define this expression and are not replaced by refitted coefficients or a newer conversion constant.
The power port is a local volumetric neutral-beam deposition power density in W/m^3. The caller supplies the slowing time in seconds; neither a volume nor a slowing-time model is inferred.
The birth-pitch input is a cosine relative to the magnetic axis, not an angle. Its equivalence to a toroidal-direction or full-local-magnetic-field pitch is not established.
Inputs are converted to real binary64 arrays without physical-domain rejection of zero, negative or nonfinite values. Such arithmetic probes do not represent qualified physical plasma states.

inputs.name: beam_mass_number
inputs.description: Beam isotope mass number A used in the E/A energy normalization.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; scalar -> (1,1), vector -> row; leading axes expand with singleton padding on the right
inputs.dtype: real scalar or array-like converted to float64; complex-valued inputs rejected
inputs.constraints: No positivity or finiteness check; the caller owns physical interpretation and compatibility with the other input axes.

inputs.name: beam_energy_ev
inputs.description: Beam-particle injection energy E, before the E/A and MeV normalizations.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; scalar -> (1,1), vector -> row; leading axes expand with singleton padding on the right
inputs.dtype: real scalar or array-like converted to float64; complex-valued inputs rejected
inputs.constraints: No positivity or finiteness check; E enters the particle-rate division even when power density is zero.

inputs.name: birth_pitch_cosine
inputs.description: Cosine of the neutral-particle birth direction relative to the magnetic axis.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; scalar -> (1,1), vector -> row; leading axes expand with singleton padding on the right
inputs.dtype: real scalar or array-like converted to float64; complex-valued inputs rejected
inputs.constraints: A cosine parameter, not degrees or radians. Arithmetic uses fmin(1,abs(value)); magnitudes above one and infinities cap at one, and NaN maps to one.

inputs.name: electron_density_m3
inputs.description: Local electron number density n in the normalization S*tau/n.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; scalar -> (1,1), vector -> row; leading axes expand with singleton padding on the right
inputs.dtype: real scalar or array-like converted to float64; complex-valued inputs rejected
inputs.constraints: No positivity, finiteness or density-threshold check; division by zero and nonfinite arithmetic are retained.

inputs.name: electron_temperature_ev
inputs.description: Electron temperature te, normalized as T=(te/1e3)/10.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; scalar -> (1,1), vector -> row; leading axes expand with singleton padding on the right
inputs.dtype: real scalar or array-like converted to float64; complex-valued inputs rejected
inputs.constraints: No positivity or finiteness check. A negative scaled temperature uses the complex fractional-power branch; zero and extreme values can give warnings and nonfinite results.

inputs.name: power_density_w_m3
inputs.description: Supplied local volumetric neutral-beam deposition power density P.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; scalar -> (1,1), vector -> row; leading axes expand with singleton padding on the right
inputs.dtype: real scalar or array-like converted to float64; complex-valued inputs rejected
inputs.constraints: Total injected power in W is not interchangeable with this port. No volume conversion, positivity check or zero-power shortcut is applied.

inputs.name: electron_slowing_time_s
inputs.description: Caller-supplied electron slowing time tau multiplying the local particle-rate density.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; scalar -> (1,1), vector -> row; leading axes expand with singleton padding on the right
inputs.dtype: real scalar or array-like converted to float64; complex-valued inputs rejected
inputs.constraints: No slowing-time estimate, clipping, positivity check or finiteness check is performed.

outputs.name: stopping_increment_m2
outputs.description: Only the empirical additive fast-ion contribution to the stopping cross section.
outputs.shape: ndarray with at least two axes, from the declared leading-axis expansion; all-scalar inputs -> (1,1)
outputs.constraints: May contain signed, NaN, infinite or complex values. Neither a finite nonnegative value nor a zero result for zero power is guaranteed.

preconditions: Supply the declared local units, the magnetic-axis birth-pitch cosine and an independently chosen electron slowing time.
Accept the fixed y=0.6 expression, real binary64 input conversion and the stated leading-axis expansion convention.
supported: Stateless evaluation of the specified empirical additive expression, with no input mutation.
Scalar, row, column, matrix and N-dimensional evaluations, including the declared arithmetic and incompatible-axis behavior.
excluded: Total stopping cross section, attenuation, energy deposition, time evolution, a slowing-time estimate or a complete application model.
Beam geometry or magnetic-field reconstruction, or equivalence of magnetic-axis, toroidal-direction and full-local-field pitch.

A quantified calibrated energy/density/pitch interval, a fit-error bound, arbitrary species coverage or independent physical validation. The qualitative low-density/high-energy context is not a calibration domain.
Parity for redundant trailing singleton axes, particular MATLAB releases or non-binary64 input-storage behavior.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises TypeError for complex-valued inputs. Values that cannot be converted to float64 propagate their conversion error; incompatible expanded axes raise ValueError.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical arithmetic may emit RuntimeWarning and return NaN, signed infinity or complex values. Zero, negative, nonfinite and extreme real values are not replaced with a fallback or rejected as unphysical; caller warning filters can turn warnings into exceptions.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is a direct stateless expression with no iteration.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial array is returned after an exception. NaN/Inf/complex entries in a returned array are retained arithmetic outcomes, not a convergence or scientific-validity status.

python.signature: evaluate_fast_ion_stopping_increment(beam_mass_number, beam_energy_ev, birth_pitch_cosine, electron_density_m3, electron_temperature_ev, power_density_w_m3, electron_slowing_time_s)

example.description: Evaluate one all-scalar case with a supplied magnetic-axis birth-pitch cosine, local power density and slowing time.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_fast_ion_stopping_increment
increment = evaluate_fast_ion_stopping_increment(1.0, 100000.0, 0.5, 1e18, 10000.0, 1e6, 1.0)
assert increment.shape == (1, 1)
np.testing.assert_allclose(increment, [[1.9645775636530587e-18]], rtol=5e-12, atol=1e-300)
print(increment.shape)
print(increment.dtype)
print(f'{increment[0, 0]:.17g} m^2')

scope: Fixed numerical baselines cover the seven ports, strict energy-ratio cutoff, absolute pitch cap, negative/zero/nonfinite arithmetic and complex-temperature results; finite real and imaginary components use rtol=5e-12 and atol=1e-300. Warnings are retained as diagnostics; equality of warning text or counts is not required.
Direct tests check scalar/row/column/matrix/N-dimensional axes, expansion, empty input and incompatible-axis failure, plus unchanged inputs.

An independent high-precision expression checks numerical evaluation, with linear scaling in power density and supplied slowing time and inverse scaling in electron density; the example checks one finite scalar case. Dimensional closure rests on the declared definitions and cited area unit, not numerical tests of physical validity.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Numerical baselines and independent expression/scaling checks support evaluation of this specified empirical relation and its declared arithmetic/axis behavior. They do not establish a calibrated physical domain, quantified fit error, general species validity or complete application behavior. The cited area scale, normalization and birth-pitch definitions do not close those gaps. Human scientific acceptance remains pending.
known_limitations: The qualitative low-density/high-energy setting supplies no quantitative density gate or calibrated energy/pitch interval; fixed y=0.6 is a model assumption.
No independent physical calibration, fit-error bound or general species coverage is established; the simplified treatment may overestimate enhancement.
The caller supplies local power density, electron slowing time and the appropriate magnetic-axis birth-pitch cosine; no conversion from total power or alternative pitch geometry is inferred.

Warnings, signed results, NaN/Inf and complex values can occur, including from finite or zero-power inputs. Redundant trailing-singleton, MATLAB-release and non-binary64-storage parity are not promised.
The generic discovery classification means no named-device constants are built in; it does not certify physical applicability.

references: K. Okano et al. (2001), ECA 25A, P2.088, pp. 809-812; birth-pitch definition on p. 810 and area scale/normalization in Eq. (6), p. 811. https://info.fusion.ciemat.es/OCS/EPS2001/pdfs/P2.088.pdf
